Subject: Discovery Recap: latency & concurrency targets (p95) — Finly

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the candid discussion on your latency pain and scale concerns. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points we heard
- User-facing chat experiences show intermittent lag: p95 text-generation latency spikes to ~1.6–2.2s during peak hours (sessions with streaming enabled).
- Concurrency: production load currently sees ~220 concurrent chat sessions at peak, trending toward 350 over next quarter.
- Streaming UX: customers expect first token within ~200–300ms and continuous token flow thereafter; current implementation has long first-token delays and occasional stalls.
- Cost sensitivity: business wants to keep inference spend growth below 2.5x YoY while improving latency.

Current stack (what you shared)
- Frontend: React-based web chat (custom websocket streaming).
- Backend: Kubernetes Fargate + managed Redis for session state.
- Model: open LLM hosted on cloud GPU endpoints; no dedicated pooling today.

Success criteria (what would make this a Win)
- p95 generation latency <= 800ms for standard prompt lengths; first-token <= 300ms for streaming flows.
- Stable support for 350 concurrent sessions with 95%+ success rate and <1% fallback to queued mode.
- Cost per 1k tokens reduced by at least 20% through batching/caching/quantization recommendations.

Proposed next steps
1) Share a lightweight telemetry checklist (metrics + sample traces) — we listed required traces and token-level timing keys in the attached PDF.
2) Run a short focused POC: 48–72h load test against a dedicated Redwood pool (we can simulate your concurrency and streaming pattern).
3) If POC meets success criteria, propose a dedicated pilot (reserved capacity) with canary rollout.

Attachments: finly-discovery-notes-20261110.pdf — short checklist and measurement guidance.

I'll loop in Aditya to coordinate the POC configuration and calendar invites.

Thanks,

— Marissa

Thanks Marissa — adding a few technical notes from our infra side to help prep the POC. Samir, quick confirmations below will speed setup.

Technical notes / assumptions
- We'll provision a dedicated pool of GPUs with continuous-batching enabled and streaming-optimized kernels.
- For streaming first-token targets (~200–300ms), we recommend running with sequence caching and smaller initial chunk sizes (512 tokens window).
- For p95 targets <=800ms, we expect to need a combination of: optimized kernels, increased concurrency per instance, and prefix KV caching for repeated prompt patterns.
- We'll instrument per-token timing (client receive timestamp + server emit timestamp) and a small tracer to capture stall events.

Questions for Finly (Samir)
- Can you share a sample 1-hour synthetic trace (curl or websocket) that reproduces the peak concurrency pattern?
- Are there any prompt pre/post-processing steps on your side that add >50ms before sending to the model?

POC logistics
- We can start the 48h load run as early as Thursday (11/12) if we get the telemetry artifacts by EOD tomorrow (11/11).
- We'll record a demo and share a short clip (demo-recording-20261111.mp4) and a post-POC report.

Happy to sync quickly to go over the telemetry checklist — I'll set a 20-minute tech sync once Samir confirms availability.

— Aditya
